fixedRegulatoryDates.title: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations apply
fixedRegulatoryDates.obligation: Disclose AI interaction to users; label synthetic/AI-generated content; deepfake identification. Applies to ANY in-scope AI system, not only high-risk. For an AAC predictor, the relevant question is whether output meets the synthetic-content marking trigger.
fixedRegulatoryDates.action: Date PASSED 2026-08-02 (verified 2026-08-09 against Commission FAQ). 50(2) marking on prod (lib/art50_marker.rb). 50(1) disclosure UI is BUILT but article_50_disclosure remains AVAILABLE-only. Ongoing: (1) Scot decision to enable for EU accounts or record dated non-applicability rationale; (2) clear pre-enable WCAG High LL-a9d6d5a46b; (3) keep DOC-771d214850 plan current. Machine-readable marking grace for 50(2) ends 2026-12-02 (fix-euaiact-art50-2-2026-12-02) and is not headroom for first EU placement after 2026-08-02.

fixedRegulatoryDates.title: EU AI Act Article 50(2) machine-readable marking grace ends
fixedRegulatoryDates.obligation: The 2026-12-02 grace on the Article 50(2) machine-readable marking sub-obligation comes from the Digital Omnibus on AI AMENDING regulation (Council final adoption 2026-06-29; OJ publication expected July 2026, in force 3 days after publication), not the original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Two conditions our earlier note missed: (a) the grace defers ONLY 50(2) marking -- 50(1)/(3)/(4)/(5) remain live for 2026-08-02; (b) it applies ONLY to AI systems already placed on the EU market before 2026-08-02. A system first placed on the EU market from 2026-08-02 onward must mark immediately, with no grace.
fixedRegulatoryDates.action: NOT headroom for LingoLinq. Applicability decided 2026-07-13 (AI_GOVERNANCE_MEMO section 5.2, pending re-attestation): board gen / focus words / eval narration are in-scope and already marked + on prod (PR #584), so they need no grace; word prediction is out of 50(2) scope via the assistive-function carve-out. LingoLinq has no pre-2026-08-02 EU deployment, so any first EU deployment is a 'new' system with no December grace. Re-verify Digital Omnibus OJ publication directly at EUR-Lex before citing this date to counsel or a customer.
